- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward slightly to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently overcorrects after strong upward moves (e.g., >72.5), leading to overshoots in next period; cap forecast at +2–3% above recent peak if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- In low-sentiment environments (sentiment <0.3), model underestimates mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for lagged rebound.
- If 3–5 consecutive days of low sentiment + falling prices, model tends to ignore trend; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to capture potential reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 0.5–1.5% to final 5–7 days if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model lags in adjusting; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% in next 3–5 days to capture sentiment momentum.
